# 1.35.0 Beta 2: Rosa comes alive, and SynGuard asks instead of blocking

The one-time reset of model selections from Beta 1 does not happen again: models you have chosen
since then stay as they are.

## SynGuard asks when it cannot check

- In Beta 1 a failed Decisions check silently blocked every write in the round: without an
  OpenRouter key, on a network error or when the model gave no answer, the agent could not
  change anything. Now SynGuard decides for each call separately. Only an explicit "unsafe"
  answer from a Decisions model blocks a call without asking. When a Decisions check fails or
  gives no answer, the write does not run on its own: you are asked, and the question says that
  SynGuard did not check it. Reading is never held up.
- New files in Downloads and on the Desktop, and documents the AI created, still need no
  approval, even when the protection model would ask for one.
- The audit log marks calls blocked by SynGuard reliably.
- Settings are read once at start, not twice.

## Rosa: fixes

- He no longer stands on the tip of his tail when scared or angry. He stands on his hind paws,
  with his tail up and puffed.
- His tail is no longer cut off by the edge of his picture.
- Swinging him by the scruff works like a pendulum: his body trails behind your hand instead of
  flying ahead of it.
- Covering his eyes no longer draws a face over his paws.
- His spending is now estimated on providers that do not report prices themselves (OpenAI,
  Anthropic and others).
- His words no longer assume your gender, and calling him back no longer makes him resentful
  when he was not.

## Rosa: clearer feelings

Every feeling now has a face, a small icon in a bubble over his head, a pose and sometimes an
effect, and replies from his own model are shown the same way. Scared, he crouches and trembles,
with waves around his body, and a real fright sends him behind the message box. Angry, his tail
bristles.

## Rosa: he sits anywhere

He stays where you put him: anywhere along the message box, on the settings card, on top of the
bottom block of the chat list or at the bottom of the window. At the bottom he settles in a free
gap and never covers the buttons. He no longer walks home on his own; moving somewhere else is
his own idea.

## Rosa: a life of his own

- Left alone, he finds something to do: lies down and wags his tail, moves to another spot,
  struts like on a catwalk, chases his own tail until he is dizzy, turns his back and wiggles his
  rear to tease you, sits by the cursor and begs for attention, or invites you to play.
- One such thing every minute or two at most, and never while you type, read a dialog, work in
  the chat list or use another window. Teasing and begging happen only with **Mischief** on. With
  animations off he only changes his pose.

## Rosa: games

- **Fetch.** He brings the ball himself, drops it by the cursor and waits. Click or throw it;
  ignore it and he takes it away.
- **Hide and seek.** He peeks out from behind the message box in different places. Click him to
  find him.
- **Tag.** He runs from the cursor along the edge. Click him to catch him.
- **Fight.** Dart the cursor back and forth under his nose and he fights it with his paws.
- Hide and seek and tag are also in his menu. Esc or picking him up ends a game.

## Rosa: the big bite

Annoy him enough and he lunges at the cursor: two big rows of see-through teeth snap shut over
it. A cold Rosa bites a cursor that lingers on him; an angry one bites when you boop his nose,
tug his tail or tease him.

## Rosa: he may refuse to come

If he ran off offended, **Call Rosa** may not bring him back: he shouts something rude from
behind the edge, with asterisks, and stays away. The third call always brings him back, and if
you hid him yourself, he comes at once. Bites and refusals go into his diary.

## Menu icons

The sorting items of the chat list menu have icons, with the check mark on the right. Rosa's
menu has icons too; they are loaded only when you open it.
